headline: Approved $12,931,640 airport checkpoint contract, planning fees starting November 2, and $105,000 for three nonprofits.
summary: An ordinance removing floor area ratio from the Downtown Development District passed 8-0. A change to the remote participation policy passed 6-2, and two special amusement permits were approved. Residents also spoke about homelessness, addiction, and funding for warming centers.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 14, 2026 regular meeting.
Approved authorizing the execution of a municipal bill of sale for real estate at 8 H Street.
Approved a $12,931,640 contract with Sheridan Corporation for the TSA security screening checkpoint expansion at Bangor International Airport.
Approved buying a 2028 tandem axle plow truck for Public Works from Freightliner & Western Star of Maine for $273,902.
Approved appointing Grace Innis as interim City Solicitor.
Held first reading of a resolve appropriating $222,040 in Customer Facility Charge funds for planning the consolidated rental car facility.
Held first reading of a resolve appropriating up to $65,000 from undesignated fund balance to fund a Director of Transit.
Passed an ordinance removing floor area ratio from the Downtown Development District, 8-0.
Approved accepting and appropriating $823,851 for the Nourish ME Rural Nutrition Education Program from the University of New England.
Approved accepting and appropriating up to $6,000 from Johns Hopkins University for a National Institutes for Health ARISE grant on PrEP access.
Approved a special amusement permit for Scoreboard Social LLC d/b/a Benjamin's Restaurant & Pub at 123 Franklin Street.
Approved a special amusement permit for Penobscot Theatre Company at 131 Main Street.
Approved amending the Remote Participation Policy, 6-2.
Approved an amendment by substitution to the order adding new planning fees, 7-0.
Approved the order adding new planning fees starting November 2, 2026, as amended, 7-0.
Approved directing up to $105,000 in Bangor Community Development Block Grant funds to Bangor Public Health and Community Services to fund three nonprofit organizations, 5-2.

MINUTES OF REGULAR MEETING BANGOR CITY COUNCIL- OCTOBER 26, 2026
Meeting called to order at 7: 00 PM
Chaired by Council Chair Hawes
Councilors Present: Beck, Deane, Faloon, Fish, Leonard,
Mallar, Walker, Hawes
Councilors Absent: Carson
Meeting adjourned at 9:15 PM
RECOGNITION Recognized the Dedication of Tony Bernatche' s Volunteerism Each Year with the
Greater Bangor July 4"` Corporation
PROCLAMATION Proclaimed October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month
PUBLIC COMMENT Scott Pardy thanked the Council for their service. He also spoke regarding the need to
address addiction and the dysfunction of the Homelessness Committee.
Grace Nichols also spoke about homelessness and the needfor more State funding.
Robin Perkinsthankedthe Councilfor their effortsto makeBangor a betterplace and
felt the quiet majority appreciate their willingness to serve.
Eden Saylor was in favor of funding for warming centers.
ReesePerkins stated he as served on several committeesfor 14years and progress
begins when we ask what we can do to help. He felt there needed to be more
volunteers to make Bangor a better place.
Jody MacDonald felt everyone should be treated as a human being, there needed to be
a change in the tax structure and Bangor police needed to be supported
Seth D., Pastor, spoke on the importance for emergency funding for warming centers.
Mike Gendreau also spoke regarding the needfor warming centers.
